 Thanksgiving Travel 2026: A Little Planning Goes a Long Way at BGR
 November 18, 2026 
 Posted in
 Easy-peasy Travel 
 Family Trips 
 Millions of Americans are preparing to travel for Thanksgiving, and Bangor International Airport is helping passengers get a head start on a smoother holiday journey. 
 Thanksgiving is almost here, and whether you’re flying across the country to gather with family, welcoming loved ones home to Maine, or escaping to somewhere a little warmer, one thing is certain: you won’t be traveling alone!
 According to AAA’s 2026 Thanksgiving travel forecast , approximately 81.5 million Americans are expected to travel 50 miles or more from home between November 24 and November 30. That includes nearly 6 million domestic air travelers heading through airports nationwide.
 While those numbers are slightly below last year’s record-setting holiday, Thanksgiving remains one of the busiest travel periods of the year.
 At Bangor International Airport (BGR), we’re looking forward to welcoming holiday travelers through our terminal. And while we can’t help you decide who’s bringing the pumpkin pie, we can offer a few tips to help make your journey a little less stressful.
 The Thanksgiving Travel Rush: What to Expect
 Thanksgiving travel isn’t limited to the day before the holiday. Airports across the country experience increased passenger traffic as families and friends make their way to holiday gatherings and return home afterward.
 Historically, the Wednesday before Thanksgiving and the Sunday following the holiday are among the busiest days for air travel. In fact, the Sunday after Thanksgiving in 2025 set a national record , with more than 3.1 million passengers screened at TSA checkpoints.
 For passengers flying from Bangor, it’s important to remember that even if your departure airport feels manageable, your connecting airport may be experiencing significantly higher passenger volumes.
 A little extra preparation before leaving home can make a big difference.
 Arrive Early. Seriously, Two Hours Early.
 We know. You’ve flown out of BGR before, and sometimes you’ve been through security in just a few minutes.
 But holiday travel is not the time to test your personal airport arrival record!
 BGR recommends arriving at least two hours before your scheduled departure. 
 That gives you time to park, check your bags, visit the airline ticket counter if needed, clear TSA security screening, and make your way to your gate.
 Remember, your flight’s departure time is not the same as its boarding time. Airlines begin boarding well before departure and close their boarding doors before the aircraft leaves the gate.
 Give yourself the gift of a little extra time. It’s much more enjoyable to relax at your gate than to race through the terminal worrying about missing your flight.
 Pack Smart, Especially if Thanksgiving Dinner Is Coming Along
 Bringing Grandma’s famous stuffing? A homemade pumpkin pie? Maybe you’ve been assigned the all-important task of transporting the gravy?
 Before packing your Thanksgiving favorites, take a moment to review TSA’s food guidelines.
 Generally, solid foods such as pies, cakes, breads, and cooked turkey can travel in carry-on bags, subject to security screening. Foods that can be poured, spread, sprayed, or spilled, including gravy, cranberry sauce, and certain casseroles, may be subject to the 3.4-ounce liquids rule when packed in carry-on luggage.
 Larger quantities of those items should generally go in checked baggage.
 Not sure about a particular dish? TSA has a handy “What Can I Bring?” tool at TSA.gov to help you determine how to pack it.
 A little homework now could save you from having to say goodbye to that container of homemade gravy at the checkpoint, and nobody wants that kind of Thanksgiving heartbreak.
 Keep Your Identification and Travel Documents Handy
 One of the easiest ways to keep your airport experience moving smoothly is to have your identification ready when you reach the airline ticket counter or TSA checkpoint.
 Adult passengers traveling domestically should make sure they have a REAL ID-compliant driver’s license or another form of TSA-accepted identification, such as a valid passport.
 If you’re traveling internationally, check your passport and destination entry requirements well before departure, and remember to double-check your airline reservation to make sure your name matches your travel documents.
 Check Your Flight Before Leaving Home
 November weather in Maine can be unpredictable, and conditions elsewhere in the country can affect flights even when the skies over Bangor are clear.
 A delay in New York, Philadelphia, Washington, or another connecting city can have an impact on your travel plans.
 Before heading to BGR, check your flight status directly with your airline. Downloading your airline’s mobile app is also a great way to receive notifications about schedule changes, gate assignments, and boarding information.
 If you’re making a connection, keep an eye on that flight, too.
 And if weather or other disruptions affect your itinerary, your airline is your best resource for rebooking and updated flight information.
 Slow Down Around the Terminal and Parking Areas
 The holiday travel rush doesn’t begin at the TSA checkpoint. It starts before you even walk through our terminal doors.
 With travelers arriving, departing, parking, and picking up loved ones, the roadways and parking areas around BGR can be busier than usual.
 Please drive slowly, watch for pedestrians, follow posted signs, and use extra caution in our parking lots and along the terminal access road.
 If you’re picking someone up, check their flight status before heading to the airport and coordinate your pickup plans in advance.
 A little patience and courtesy go a long way toward keeping everyone safe.
 Remember, You’re Not the Only One Traveling
 Thanksgiving is a wonderful time to reconnect with family and friends, but getting everyone where they need to go takes a tremendous amount of coordination.
 From airline employees and TSA officers to airport operations, maintenance crews, dispatchers, and the many other professionals working behind the scenes, airport teams are helping travelers reach their destinations throughout the holiday.
 A little kindness and patience can make a big difference, especially when travel plans don’t go exactly as expected.
 While we can’t guarantee that your connecting flight will be on time, your luggage will be the first off the carousel, or your favorite Thanksgiving side dish will survive the trip, we can promise that our team is working to make your experience at BGR as welcoming as possible.
 Picking Someone Up for Thanksgiving? 
 If you’re heading to BGR to welcome family or friends home for the holiday, check their flight status before leaving the house. Arrival times can change, especially when weather or delays affect connecting airports. Coordinate your pickup plans in advance, follow posted signs, and remember to keep terminal roadways clear for other travelers.
 For your convenience, please use the free cell phone parking area on Godfrey Boulevard if you are picking up passengers and you do not plan to come into the building to meet them. Just pull to the designated area on Godfrey and wait for a call or text from your arriving passengers. Drivers must remain with their vehicle at all times.
 And when that long-awaited reunion finally happens? Well, we happen to think there’s nothing quite like a welcome home in Bangor.
 From Our BGR Family to Yours
 Thanksgiving is about the people and places that matter most. Whether your travels take you away from Maine or bring you home to it, we’re grateful to be part of the journey.
 Plan ahead, pack smart, arrive early, and give yourself a little extra time to enjoy the trip.
 After all, the best part of Thanksgiving travel is getting to the people waiting for you at the other end.
 From all of us at Bangor International Airport, safe travels and Happy Thanksgiving! 
 You pack the suitcase, we’ll get you there.
